title: Square up a racked face frame by its diagonal
instruction: The glued-up face frame on the bench is racked out of square. Make it square, so that its two corner-to-corner diagonals are equal, keep it on its outline, then let go of it.
context: Cabinetmakers and bench carpenters (O*NET 51-7011.00, 47-2031.00) check a glued-up frame by measuring its two diagonals and squeeze the long one, pushing its two corners toward each other, before the glue sets. It differs from squaring a rigid beam between guide rails or pushing a part in evenly: here the part itself changes shape under two opposed forces on different members, and a single push only slides it.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Pine face frame, 0.30 kg, outer 16 deep x 30 wide: two 3 x 3 cm rails 30 cm long running left to right, near rail centred x 20.0 and far rail centred x 33.0, and two 3 cm wide, 1 cm high stiles between them at y +-13.5, with darker 3 cm corner blocks at the four rail ends. Each of the four joints is a stub tenon (8 mm thick, 25 mm wide, 12 mm long) in a mortise with 0.2 mm side clearance, spread with PVA wood glue that is still wet, so the frame racks when the far rail is pushed along its length with about 2 N; the stiles' shoulders close against the rails when the frame is square and stop it 0.5 mm past square. The far rail starts 8 mm to the left of the near rail (y +0.8), so the diagonal from near-right to far-left is 14 mm longer than the other. Friction on the table 0.3. A yellow tape rectangle (0.4 cm wide) is stuck on the table 2 cm outside the outline of the squared frame, centred x 26.5, y 0.
scoring: Measured with a tape and a ruler. diff = difference between the two diagonals (corner block centres) at the end. 0 at once and for good if a corner is ever lifted more than 1 cm, any outer corner leaves the tape rectangle, or the far rail is pushed 15 mm from square (joint broken open). Otherwise 0 if diff is over 8 mm, 0.25 for 5 to 8 mm, 0.5 for 2 to 5 mm, and 0.5 for 2 mm or less until both grippers are at least 3 cm from the frame and it has moved less than 1 mm for 1 s; then 1.0.
reset_notes: Pull the joints apart, wipe them and spread a fresh thin film of PVA wood glue (or, for repeated trials, the same amount of white lithium grease) on all four tenons; push the frame together until the shoulders touch. Check the shear resistance with a spring scale hooked on the far rail's end while the near rail is held: it should start to slide at 1.5 to 2.5 N; thin or thicken the film until it does. Push the far rail back 8 mm to the left of the near rail (check with a ruler against the near rail's end), and set the frame inside the tape rectangle with its rails parallel to the tape.
fidelity: The glued frame is a four-bar linkage modelled as one slider: the far rail slides along y on the near rail (15 mm out to the left, 0.5 mm of play past square) with 2 N of Coulomb friction, and the stiles are hinges turned to match. The stiles are 1 cm high so the open fingers clear them. Rigid parts, friction 0.3 on the table.
